title: Tamil Nadu Politics – Evening Brief – 31 October 2026
headline: DMK women cadre protest across Tamil Nadu over price rise, law and order

sections.big_picture: Key developments in this 12-hour briefing include: DMK women cadre protest across Tamil Nadu over price rise, law and order; Theni jailbreak: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay orders suspension of Theni district jail superintendent in-charge; Tamil Nadu CM Vijay announces 3% DA hike for 16 lakh employees, pensioners ahead of Deepavali; AMMK Dhinakaran targets Vijay govt over power cuts, questions energy minister's continuance.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay cracks down after 17 prisoners break out of Theni sub-jail; deputy jailor suspended, senior officials transferred
sources.snippet: Chennai's Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has ordered the suspension of the deputy jail superintendent in charge of Thekkampatti sub-jail. This action stems from significant security lapses that allowed 17 prisoners to escape after overpowering guards. The Tamil Nadu Police quickly recaptured all escapees through a coordinated operation, which included using drones. The government has also initiated severe punitive measures against negligent prison personnel and transferred several senior officials.

top_developments.headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay announces 3% DA hike for 16 lakh employees, pensioners ahead of Deepavali
top_developments.summary: Tamil Nadu's chief minister Joseph Vijay announced a 3% increase in Dearness Allowance for employees and pensioners. The hike will raise the allowance from 60% to 63%, effective retroactively from July 1. This change aligns the state government’s DA with the recent increase for central government employees. Around 16 lakh individuals will benefit from this 3% increase in Dearness Allowance.

top_developments.headline: AMMK Dhinakaran targets Vijay govt over power cuts, questions energy minister's continuance
top_developments.summary: T T V Dhinakaran has publicly confronted the Tamil Nadu government for persistent power outages he attributes to gross administrative incompetence. He pointed out chronic issues like sudden power cuts and billing discrepancies, which significantly impact residents. Citing the outage at Meenakshi Amman temple as a critical example, Dhinakaran demanded urgent reforms in the electricity sector and called on Chief Minister Joseph Vijay to take decisive action against negligent officials.

all_sources.snippet: No vehicles will be allowed to transport minerals without GPS devices installed by November 1. The devices must be integrated with the state's MiMAS portal for real-time location tracking. Currently, around 1.10 lakh vehicles are registered, but only 50,000 actively transport minerals. Lorry owners must purchase devices from approved vendors, with costs now around ₹4000. Failure to comply will result in legal action against lorry owners.

all_sources.title: ED uncovers Rs 400 crore fund diversion by Dream Makers Global, attaches assets worth Rs 85 crore
all_sources.snippet: Enforcement Directorate has provisionally attached assets worth Rs 85.19 crore linked to Dream Makers Global Pvt Ltd. This action is associated with an alleged investment fraud involving thousands of depositors and high-return promises. The investigation revealed that Rs 400 crore was collected from investors through misleading schemes. Funds were misappropriated, with heavy commissions paid to agents and key personnel.
